text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1816007777 - elevated GPU queue for customer acme-payments (private VPC). cluster=acme-pay-01, gpu_util=95%, queue=420, autoscaler errors detected. paging oncall.
Maya: Ack. I'm taking it. @ryan @priya standby.
Maya: quick checklist: runbook -> https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale 
Maya: `kubectl top nodes` shows GPUs @ ~96-99%.
Maya: checking autoscaler logs: `scaleLoop: failed to create node: quotaExceeded` and `APIError: InsufficientIPs`. looks like network/NAT or cloud quota.
infra-bot: autoscaler snapshot: `APIError: InsufficientIPs: cannot allocate`. request-id=e-46f2a.
Ryan: tried manual scale from private-console, got `ClusterCapacityLimitReached` (node_pool.max=12).
Priya: acme-payments node_pool.max is 12 per contract. can't exceed without customer approval.
Maya: queue climbing: now 487. clients seeing `429` + timeouts.
Jonathan: scope — is this isolated to acme-payments private cluster or broader?
Maya: isolated to their private VPC cluster. hosted tenants unaffected.
Priya: paging CSM for emergency approval. @Amanda can you help with customer comms?
Amanda: calling customer now. asking for emergency +4 nodes for 2hrs. will report back.
Linda: node events show repeated `ImagePullBackOff` and cloud logs indicate NAT SNAT port exhaustion for that VPC. nodes are failing to finish bootstrap.
Maya: so node create requests retry and then autoscaler hits quota/timeouts. that explains `quotaExceeded`.
Ryan: confirmed nodes stuck in Provisioning >7m then terminated. autoscaler backoff kicks in.
Maya: mitigation plan (short): 1) apply emergency admission throttle for non-critical requests 2) request customer node_pool increase 3) triage NAT/registry path 4) alt-bootstrap for immediate nodes if safe
Maya: applying ingress throttle to drop low-priority models. `kubectl apply -f /ops/rate-limits/emergency-throttle.yaml` -> applied. expect non-critical queue to drop ~30s.
Priya: CS informed. Customer approved emergency +2 nodes for now (not +4).
Ryan: cloud accepted node request for +2 but provisioning still failing due to registry/NAT.
infra-bot: NAT allocation metric: SNAT ports used 99.7% for acme-pay-01. new NAT requested. provisioning ETA ~6-10m.
Linda: as temporary workaround I'll bootstrap 2 nodes using alternate bootstrap image and a different mirror to avoid SNAT path.
Linda: command run: ```cloudctl create-node --cluster acme-pay-01 --image alt-bootstrap:v2 --labels=bootstrap=alt```
Linda: nodes reached Ready in ~2m and registered GPUs.
Ryan: autoscaler now sees +2 nodes. queue dropped 487->312.
Maya: good, but still short. customer only allowed +2. we need to divert critical traffic to hosted fallback.
Jonathan: drafting a fallback routing policy (critical->hosted-fallback, non-critical->throttled). pushing edge config now.
Amanda: customer consented to hosted-fallback for critical inference. logged in CS ticket #7892.
Jonathan: routing policy pushed. about ~18% of traffic rerouted to hosted-fallback.
Maya: confirm hosted pool health?
infra-bot: hosted-fallback pool: +10% utilization, no errors, accepting traffic.
Priya: customer impact update: approx 30% of requests failing for private cluster; median tail latency rose from 60ms -> 2.4s. CS updated.
Maya: oncall handoff in 15m to Jonathan. summary for handoff: root cause = SNAT port exhaustion + intermittent registry mirror causing node bootstrap failures -> autoscaler perceived quota/limit errors. mitigations applied: emergency throttle, alt-bootstrap +2 nodes, hosted-fallback routing, NAT scale request, customer approved +2.
Jonathan: taking over. I'll monitor queue, follow infra for NAT scaling, and own post-incident tasks.
Maya: leaving followups: 1) validate registry mirror redundancy 2) recommend increasing per-VPC SNAT port pool or add NAT autoscaling 3) tweak autoscaler to ignore transient image pull errors for short window (3m) 4) cost/impact calc and customer communication draft.
Maya: assigning postmortem to eng-infra and eng-runtime; ticket INC-2026-324 created by incident-bot (severity S2).
Jonathan: will open a war room if provisioning regressions reappear. switching to eng-oncall channel for next hour.
Amanda: customer confirmed critical path recovery; they requested a follow-up tomorrow on hard limits and SLA implications.
Maya: handing off. thanks team. :heart:
incident-bot: incident INC-2026-324 declared. tracking enabled.
Jonathan: monitoring. will update last_message_ts on close.
